proposedOverrides.name: Amazonian societies (regional overview)
proposedOverrides.summary: A broad regional map category covering diverse Amazonian histories. Named archaeological sites reveal forest and river foraging, early cultivation, pottery and later earthworks; they do not define a single people or state.

scopeNotes: The imported record spans 1500 BCE to 1800 CE but its polygons change and extend beyond a precise Amazon basin boundary. It is a broad classificatory overlay, not an ethnic group or polity. The display name and authored summary replace the misleading implication that all people in this area were exclusively hunter-gatherers.

Named case studies span different periods and subregions. The card does not certify that every site lies inside every snapshot, that all populations shared the same lifeway, or that present communities can automatically be assigned to ancient deposits.

The Pedra Pintada research abstract was read in the USF repository. No exact occupation dates, species list or painting attribution beyond its abstract are asserted. A separate NPS PDF download failed and was not used.

The 2013 PLOS shell-midden paper was read, including faunal analysis, discussion and figures’ captions. Burnt shells, impact-fractured deer bone, charcoal and chemical evidence jointly support anthropogenic deposition. The analysis explicitly allows snail consumption to have been supplementary, and seasonality remains an interpretation.

The 2020 Nature main text is subscription content; its abstract, figure captions and extended-data descriptions were available and read. Plant identifications, named sites and dated occurrences come from those accessible portions. Calibrated BP refers to 1950; the approximate 8400 to 4900 BCE phase brackets the reported 10350 to 6850 cal BP crop attestations, not a polity lifetime.

The 2018 earthwork paper’s indexed results were read after direct access failures. Mt-04 is not conflated with the larger Z-Mt-04 compound. Charcoal near basal ceramics supports the reported date range; neither a ditch nor a burning layer identifies warfare or an attacker. Geometric enclosure traditions differ across regions.

The 2022 dark-earth response was read with the competing 2021 hypothesis identified. The card reports physical contexts that support anthropic formation, not a claim that all fertility everywhere has one origin. The 2023 study’s ancient intentionality argument is presented as a comparison-based interpretation.

Kuikuro history is one named example, not a template projected across all Amazonian communities. The ISA account’s blanket claim to unique continuity in the Amazon and its exact population estimates are not repeated. No single epidemic date or conquest is imposed on the entire region.
Imported geometry remains unverified. No successor link is appropriate for the regional classification. Independent historical review and depth certification remain pending.
